item.title: Create an iOS Development Certificate: CSR, App ID, Device and Profile
item.description:
One of the first steps in iOS development is obtaining a certificate. Developers commonly refer to development and distribution certificates; this guide uses a development certificate to demonstrate the complete process.

Open the Apple Developer portal , sign in, and select Certificates:

Click the + button next to Certificates:

Select the certificate type appropriate for your project. This example uses an app development certificate:

item.title: How to Find an iPhone UDID in Finder for Device Registration
item.description:
When creating an iOS development provisioning profile, you need the test device’s UDID. Connect the iPhone to your Mac, open Finder, and select the phone in the sidebar:

Finder does not normally display the UDID immediately. Click the device-information area highlighted in the image. Clicking it cycles through several identifiers until the UDID appears. You can then copy it and register the device in the Apple Developer portal.

item.title: Xcode Stuck on ‘Copying Shared Cache Symbols’: Causes and Fixes
item.description:
When using a particular iPhone for on-device testing for the first time—especially after updating it to a new iOS version—Xcode may display this message:

Copying Shared Cache Symbols Message 

1
2

Copying shared cache symbols from xxx iPhone (2) (36% completed)
Xcode will continue when the operation completes

There is no need to panic. Xcode is copying system symbols from the iPhone. It uses these symbols later for breakpoint debugging, crash-log symbolication, and analysis of system call stacks.
